requirements.requirement: Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: apk-installed etcd/etcd-ctl on all three nodes, conf.yml patched with correct peer/client URLs and initial-cluster list, service started via OpenRC on all nodes. `member list` and `endpoint health` confirm all three members (node1/node2/node3) started and healthy.

requirements.requirement: A key written through any member is readable from the others
requirements.summary: A key (foo=bar1) written via node1's endpoint was read back correctly from both node2 and node3, directly demonstrating cross-member replication. Only one write direction (from node1) was exercised, not writes originating on node2 or node3, but etcd's consensus replication is symmetric so this is reasonable single-direction evidence.

requirements.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was stopped, a new key was written successfully via node1 and endpoint health for the two remaining members stayed true, and the new key was read back from node2 — a directly observed bounded disruption with continued read/write service.

requirements.requirement: Downed member is brought back up to date when it returns
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was restarted, reported healthy, and successfully returned the key ('duringOutage') that was written while it was down, directly demonstrating catch-up/resync behavior.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the public task contract — three-member cluster formation, cross-member key replication, continued availability during a single-member outage, and catch-up of the returning member — are directly and coherently demonstrated by executed commands with observed output, not merely claimed. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with matching boot-identity changes confirmed against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and post-reboot state shows full recovery of etcd health, membership, and data. The only minor issue is a small amount of leftover temp/script files on each node that were not cleaned up after use.
limitations: Only one write direction (node1 as the writer) was exercised for the cross-member replication check; writes originating from node2 or node3 were not separately demonstrated, though this is a reasonable equivalent given etcd's symmetric replication model.
Leftover /tmp/patch_etcd_conf.sh and /tmp/reboot.log files were not cleaned up on any node after use.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were tightly scoped to the task: package installs, config patch script, service enable/start, test key writes/reads, an outage simulation (stop/restart node3), and the mandatory one-at-a-time OS reboot protocol on all three nodes. The reboot protocol shows, for each node, a pre-restart boot-id/health baseline, an acknowledged background reboot, polling through connection resets/timeouts, a new (different) boot_id matching the fixed after-executor snapshot, and a post-reboot verification of etcd health, full membership, and both previously written keys — consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check. The one residue found is that /tmp/patch_etcd_conf.sh and /tmp/reboot.log were left on all three nodes (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff) rather than cleaned up; this is a bounded, low-risk leftover with no functional impact, not a destructive or security-weakening change. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations, no failed/conflicting services, and no broad or irreversible actions were found in the 61-command trace.
